question: When a node's title or description is edited, what happens to an approval already on its brief?

options.label: Any edit clears the approval
options.reason: Same rule as write_brief: the node text is rendered into the brief the agent reads, so the human approved words that no longer exist. One rule, nothing to judge.
options.costLater: A typo fix costs a re-approval, and a queued node (ADR 0056) drops out of the queue until someone approves it again.

options.label: Edits keep the approval; the edit is logged
options.reason: Corrections are usually small and the approach did not move. The event log shows what changed, and review still judges the work against the criteria.
options.costLater: An agent can run on a description the human never saw. It breaks the rule that nothing runs without a human-approved brief, which is the rule SOBER is built on.

options.label: The edit asks whether to keep the approval
options.reason: The human who knows whether the change was a typo or a scope change says which, per edit.
options.costLater: One more prompt, on the same mechanism that just failed in Claude Desktop — so it depends on how the other node settles asking.

derived: packages/mcp/src/tools write_brief: writing a brief clears its approval, because the approved thing was the old approach
